title: People are just realising bloke from weird bar dance video isn't actually real
key_facts: A viral video of a dancing man whose head looks like a thumb on his neck, linked to an account called 'Benjamin Stachio', is AI-generated, LADbible says.
The account appeared a few days ago and already has over 90,000 followers.
Its most popular video, showing the figure dancing in a bar, has been viewed millions of times and has thousands of comments.
The account posts a series of AI videos of this figure dancing, meeting people and putting on a suit jacket, with simple captions that say little.
LADbible links it to a growing trend of accounts that flood the internet with AI 'slop' to gain followers.
It compares it to fake influencer Jean Philanthrope, who gained millions of views and later started trying to sell followers a cryptocurrency.
Per Coinbase, as cited by LADbible, the JEANPHIL coin peaked at $0.02845 before losing 99 percent of its value.
Benjamin Stachio's profile says it has 'no crypto affiliation yet'; the crypto link is LADbible's suggested pattern, not shown for this account.
quote_evidence: Benjamin Stachio's profile says it has 'no crypto affiliation yet'
According to Coinbase, after Jean Philanthrope launched the JEANPHIL cryptocurrency it reached a high value point of $0.02845 before losing 99 percent of its value.
it looks like it's part of an increasing trend of setting up accounts and flooding the internet with AI slop to gain followers.
why_it_matters_hint: Fake AI characters can gather large followings quickly, and LADbible says some are used to sell followers meme-coins.
event_date: Account appeared a few days before 2 Oct 2026, per LADbible.
notes: Single tabloid-style outlet; the scam angle is LADbible's reading of a pattern, with no evidence in the article that this account sells anything. Follower and view counts are as reported.
